nodes.label: Icon Philosophy (Phase 1.5)
nodes.rationale: An icon is a quiet footnote subordinate to text, never an illustration; no filled/solid styles because they would outweigh the typography.

nodes.label: Texture Philosophy (Phase 1.5)
nodes.rationale: Materiality is achieved through quality of light, never applied texture; grain is explicitly excluded because it dates the interface.

nodes.label: Editorial Layout Principles (gap)
nodes.rationale: V1 applies one undifferentiated rhythm philosophy to fundamentally different page types (checkout, editorial description, admin table, About page) and never states a resumability principle for long-form content.

nodes.label: Reading-First Experience
nodes.rationale: The product's job is to shorten the distance between arrival and calm, absorbed reading; it is a reading experience that happens to have a storefront attached.

nodes.label: Luxury Interaction Philosophy (gap)
nodes.rationale: Distinct from Motion Language: no stance on intentional friction in checkout, no philosophy of forgiveness, no anticipation/attentiveness principle.

nodes.label: Motion Language (V1)
nodes.rationale: Every motion must have a plausible physical analogy (a page turning, a breath, light shifting); timing scales with the size of the change it communicates.

nodes.label: Trust Design lifecycle (gap)
nodes.rationale: V1 treats trust as static accumulation; review asks for a lifecycle view covering first visit, mid-purchase, failure recovery, and returning-customer trust.

nodes.label: Dashboard Experience Philosophy (V1)
nodes.rationale: The admin dashboard is the desk where a solo founder runs the business; calmness there is infrastructure, not decoration, because dashboard stress leaks into the reader's experience.

nodes.label: Growth Constraints (Tier 6, GC)
nodes.rationale: New features must be justified by reader effort reduction, editorial trust, or business support; checked against NNP/PIC before implementation; extend existing patterns before inventing new ones.

nodes.label: Interaction Constraints (Tier 5, IC)
nodes.rationale: No simultaneous attention-seeking animations, no autoplay by default, loading indication required, reduced-motion respected, confirmation weight proportional to reversibility.

nodes.label: Trust Constraints (Tier 2, TC)
nodes.rationale: Requires unambiguous transaction confirmation, no premature success states, actionable failure messages, minimal data collection, and same-session resolution of payment failures.

nodes.label: UX Constraints (Tier 4, UXC)
nodes.rationale: Flows completable without forced language switch, no data loss on failed submission, accessible labels, three-step navigation ceiling, WCAG AA floor.

nodes.label: Cognitive Design (gap)
nodes.rationale: Missing concepts: attention budget, visual weight as a controllable variable, noise reduction as ongoing discipline, decision fatigue per journey, and progressive complexity distinct from progressive disclosure.

nodes.label: Product Consistency & Governance (gap)
nodes.rationale: V1 lacks a precedence order among its own sections, so two designers can each correctly cite it to justify opposite decisions.

nodes.label: System Evolution Rules (gap)
nodes.rationale: No distinction between immutable core and amendable specifics, no adoption filter for future trends, no continuity mechanism for team growth.

nodes.label: Writing System Philosophy (gap)
nodes.rationale: No definition of who the English reader is, no parity rule for incomplete bilingual content, no translation-vs-transcreation stance, no mixed-script behavior.

nodes.label: Arabic Typography Philosophy
nodes.rationale: Arabic is the native language, not a localization; its own vertical rhythm, connective letterforms, and line-height relationships must be designed from first decisions, not adapted from Latin assumptions.

nodes.label: Color Philosophy (V1)
nodes.rationale: Low-saturation palette signals maturity over trend; gold functions like a gilt edge or wax seal reserved for genuine emphasis, never a decorative wash.

nodes.label: Component Philosophy (V1)
nodes.rationale: Describes intent per component family (buttons as decision points, cards as a shelf spine, forms as a notebook page) without specifying tokens or implementation.

nodes.label: Border Philosophy (Phase 1)
nodes.rationale: Learned from the Dashboard rebuild: a border marks an object, a divider marks an item within an object, whitespace marks a relationship between objects.

nodes.label: Editorial Principles (Phase 1)
nodes.rationale: States why RAQIM, even its admin, is a space you occupy (a study or atelier) rather than a SaaS dashboard you operate.

nodes.label: Color Engine (named tokens)
nodes.rationale: Names tokens by role (Canvas, Paper, Surface, Ink, Accent, Focus, Overlay, Scrim, etc.), assigning no values, so a designer reaches for a token by role, not hue.

nodes.label: Typography System (Phase 1)
nodes.rationale: Four families plus one technical face (Amiri, IBM Plex Sans Arabic, Cormorant Garamond, IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono) sharing design DNA across scripts; twelve purpose-defined type levels.

nodes.label: Product Identity Constraints (Tier 1, PIC)
nodes.rationale: Blocks convergence toward marketplace, SaaS dashboard, generic admin panel, social feed, and CMS-clone patterns (PIC-1..10).

nodes.label: Information Architecture Philosophy (gap)
nodes.rationale: V1 never states that editorial curation should always outrank algorithmic/engagement-driven sorting across the product, risking a quiet 'popular this week' feature later.

nodes.label: Editorial Identity (publishing house, not marketplace)
nodes.rationale: RAQIM behaves like a curatorial publishing house rather than a marketplace; every title carries a point of view instead of being merely listed.

nodes.label: Luxury Positioning (care, not decoration)
nodes.rationale: Luxury is defined as visible evidence of care (editing, considered covers, real translation) in a category flooded with disposable content — costs restraint, not decoration.

nodes.label: Color Philosophy (Phase 1.5)
nodes.rationale: Colors are a small number of roles, each forbidden from doing another job; Accent's authority is built on scarcity — appearing twice in the same glance loses meaning.

nodes.label: Preload + onload-swap Font Loading Strategy
nodes.rationale: preload starts the font fetch at highest priority immediately, and media=print + onload swap keep it from blocking first paint, versus a plain synchronous stylesheet link; noscript preserves original behavior with JS disabled.

nodes.label: Static SPA Deployment
nodes.rationale: Plain static SPA built with bun/vite, deployable to any static host with an SPA fallback to index.html for unknown routes.

nodes.label: Editorial Constraints (Tier 3, EC)
nodes.rationale: Requires human-authored descriptions, bilingual content parity before exposure, no promotional interstitials in reading surfaces, and human review of AI-assisted content.

nodes.label: Non-Negotiable Principles (Tier 0, NNP)
nodes.rationale: Immutable rules (NNP-1..8) that override all other tiers: reading over engagement, Arabic/RTL-first, editorial over algorithmic ordering, no manufactured urgency, one focal point, no false success states, no bilingual degradation.

nodes.label: Brand DNA (al-Raqim thesis)
nodes.rationale: Name derived from al-Raqim, the inscribed tablet of the Companions of the Cave; RAQIM is framed as being in the business of permanence, not content, for a female reader.

nodes.label: Motion Philosophy (Phase 1.5)
nodes.rationale: Motion describes behavior rather than being an effect layered on afterward; it must never simulate urgency or repeat for its own sake.
